reviews.title: The free version is actually pretty good
reviews.text: I’m only subscribed to the free version of this app but it’s actually pretty decent considering it’s free. I like the fact that it provides at least 5 different vocabulary words, with descriptive definitions that are used in sentences and also provide an audio of how to pronounce the word correctly.  After reading and learning about the definitions then you can take a quiz to test your knowledge. Once you successfully pass the quiz then you level up and start learning newer terms. It’s a good app with a really nice interface and design. It’s easy to use and I think the paid subscription is worth the money but I can’t afford to subscribe at this time. There is a free trial subscription but I’m not sure how many days it lasts.

reviews.title: a small wish
reviews.text:
I really like this App and almost use it everyday. I really miss the feature from the old version that allowed me to edit the definition and example sentence before adding a word to my Journal list. This allowed me to input the exact sentence I encountered while reading, along with the Chinese translation. Reviewing words this way made it much easier to remember their actual usage.

While I understand that quickly adding words meets the needs of some users, the old method provided a multi-layered approach that greatly helped with long-term memory. Would it be possible to add a toggle in the settings so users can choose between the "Quick Mode" and the "Classic Mode"? Thank you!

reviews.title: Not Worth Your Time
reviews.text:
I don’t understand how this app has so many positive reviews. Nothing about it is actually free. Any set of words you want to review or quiz you want to take is locked. The only way to unlock them is by watching ads, usually two. You can participate in challenges without watching an ad first, but once you finish, another ad appears.

It’s frustrating because the sets, quizzes, and challenges aren’t very time-consuming, so it feels like you’re just watching ad after ad. I’m deleting this app. I had higher hopes, but if the only way to learn anything without constant ads is by paying for a subscription ($34.99/year, $6.99/month, or $74.99 for lifetime access), I’d rather find another app that doesn’t rely so heavily on that model.
